```{=html}
<p>If the certified employee organization or organizations representing fire fighters and fire officers within the Fire Department and the employer have not reached a written agreement concerning terms and conditions of employment by March 1 of any year, either party may request arbitration by a board of arbitration, as herein provided, which request must be honored.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The board of arbitration shall be composed of 3 members, 1 appointed by the Mayor, and 1 appointed jointly by the certified employee organizations representing the fire fighters and fire officers involved.  These members shall be selected within 4 days of the request for arbitration.  The third member shall be selected within 4 additional days by the 2 arbitrators previously chosen and in accordance with the procedures of the American Arbitration Association from a list furnished by the Association.  Such member selected shall act as chairman of the board of arbitration.</p>
<p>The board of arbitration thus established shall commence the arbitration proceedings within 7 days after the chairman is selected and shall make its decision, by a majority vote, within 15 days after the commencement of the arbitration proceedings.  For good cause the chairman may extend the time requirement set forth herein.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>Within 3 days after the selection of the chairman of the board of arbitration, the Labor Commissioner or his designated representative shall provide to each member of the board of arbitration and to all parties, a detailed itemization of the last proposal made by the respective parties during the negotiations.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>The board of arbitration shall identify the major issues in the dispute, review the positions of all parties and shall take into consideration wages, benefits, hours, and other working conditions of other fire department and public safety employees in Maryland as well as in comparable metropolitan political subdivisions in other states, and shall also consider the value of other benefits available to or received by other employees of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore as compared with private sector employees in the metropolitan Baltimore City area and as compared with employees of other fire departments and other public safety employees.  The board of arbitration shall further consider consumer prices for goods and services and other related items, cost of living data, and such other factors, not confined to the foregoing, which are normally utilized in the determination of wages and other benefits in the collective bargaining process, and shall also take into account the financial condition of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>The board of arbitration shall have the power to administer oaths, compel the attendance of witnesses, and require the production of evidence by subpoena.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>The board of arbitration after hearing witnesses and considering and receiving such written evidence as may be submitted shall, by written decision, order the implementation, in its entirety, of the last proposal of one of the respective parties previously submitted in accordance with subparagraph (c) of <a href="article-ii.html#s-55">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>The decision of the majority of the board of arbitration thus established shall be final and binding upon the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore and upon the certified employee organizations involved in the proceedings.  No appeal therefrom shall be allowed.  Such decision shall constitute a mandate to the Mayor of Baltimore City in respect to such matters which can be remedied administratively by him, and as a mandate to the Board of Estimates and the City Council with respect to matter(s) which require legislative action necessary to implement the decision of the board of arbitration.</p>
<p>With respect to matters which require legislative action for implementation, such legislation shall be enacted within 45 days following the date of the arbitration decision.</p>
<p>With respect to salaries and wage scales, the amounts determined by the final decision of the board of arbitration shall be included in the proposed Ordinance of Estimates in accordance with <a href="article-vi.html#s-2">Section 2(c)(1) of Article VI</a> {<a href="article-vi.html#s-5">Article VI, § 5(a)(1)</a>}, shall not be reduced by the City Council in accordance with <a href="article-vi.html#s-2">Section 2(g) of Article VI</a> {<a href="article-vi.html#s-7">Article VI, § 7(a)(2nd par.)</a>, and shall be adopted by the Board of Estimates as the salary and wage scales for employees of the Fire Department in accordance with <a href="article-vi.html#s-5">Section 5 of Article VI</a> {<a href="article-vi.html#s-12">Article VI, § 12</a>}.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>The cost of the arbitration proceedings provided for herein shall be borne equally by the parties involved.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 704, Acts of 1985</p>
```


### § (56). Volunteer workers. {#s-56}

```{=html}
<p>To provide in its discretion such benefits as may be deemed appropriate to city volunteer workers for injury or death as a result of performing tasks assigned to them as city volunteer workers and to indemnify city volunteer workers against claims and suits under such conditions as may be prescribed.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 40, Acts of 1979</p>
```


### § (57). Loans for industrial purposes. {#s-57}

```{=html}
<p>From or in connection with funds available to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore pursuant to <a href="article-xi-i.html">Article XI-I of the Constitution of the State of Maryland</a>, to make, purchase, contract to make, or otherwise acquire financial loans to any person or other legal entity and to guarantee or insure financial loans made by third parties to any person or other legal entity, such financial loans to be used for or in connection with the purchase or acquisition of leasehold or fee simple interests in buildings or structures, and for construction, reconstruction, erection, development, rehabilitation, renovation, redevelopment or improvement of buildings or structures, located within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for industrial purposes.</p>
<p>The term “industrial purposes” shall embrace every type or branch of business, conducted for a livelihood or for profit, or conducted on a nonprofit basis, provided that the building or structure may be financed by obligations the interest on which is exempt from federal income taxation under the provisions of any federal statute, including the provisions of Section 103 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as now or hereafter amended.</p>
<p>It is hereby found and determined that conditions of unemployment exist in Baltimore City and the development of business of all types (including, without limitation, manufacturing, commerce, research, education, real estate development, and recreation) is essential to relieve this unemployment and to establish a balanced economy in Baltimore City.</p>
<p>In connection with such loans and guarantees, the City may make loans directly for qualifying projects and may guarantee or insure loans made by third parties for such projects, including loans made in the form of the acquisition by a third party of revenue bonds or any other evidence of indebtedness.</p>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 454, Acts of 1980</p>
```


### § (58). Limitations on competition. {#s-58}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Public transportation.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>It has been and shall continue to be the policy of the State to authorize Baltimore City to displace or limit competition in the area of public transportation in order to provide for adequate, economical, and efficient delivery of transportation services; to protect its citizens from inconsistent and excessive prices; to provide necessary and desired services in all areas of the City; to enable the City to provide public transportation in order to conserve energy and reduce air pollution, congestion, traffic hazards, and accidents; to encourage the use of public transportation by the contribution by the City of capital and operating funds to enable transportation to be provided at the lowest cost to all citizens, especially the indigent; and to promote the general welfare by conducting a comprehensive transportation system.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Baltimore City has the authority to grant one or more franchises for a transportation system on an exclusive or nonexclusive basis, to impose franchise fees, to establish certain rates, to establish rules, regulations, and licensing requirements to govern the operation of the franchises, and for the enforcement of any such measure, and to conduct a public transportation system on an exclusive basis, including the establishment of rules, regulations, and rates, notwithstanding any anticompetitive effect.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Water and sewerage systems; Waste collection and disposition.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>It has been and shall continue to be the policy of the State to authorize Baltimore City to displace or limit competition in the area of water and sewerage systems in order to assure delivery of adequate, economical, and efficient services to its citizens, to avoid duplication of facilities, to provide for the health and safety of its citizens, to control disease, to prevent blight and other environmental degradation, to utilize efficiently the public right-of-way, to protect limited natural resources for the benefit of the citizens of the City; and to promote the general health and welfare by providing for adequate water and sewerage systems.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>Baltimore City has the authority to grant one or more franchises or enter into contracts for water and sewerage systems on an exclusive or nonexclusive basis to any person, to impose franchise fees, to establish certain rates and charges, to establish rules, regulations, and licensing requirements, and to provide for the enforcement of any such measure notwithstanding any anticompetitive effect.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>In the event that Baltimore City has the enabling authority granted by any other law to operate water and sewerage systems, such systems shall be operated by the City without regard to any anticompetitive effect.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>It has been and shall continue to be the policy of the State that Baltimore City is directed and authorized to exercise all powers regarding waste collection and disposal notwithstanding any anticompetitive effect. This subsection does not apply to any portion of a generator’s waste which is directed by the generator to a specific facility for reuse, reclamation or recycling, or for disposal on its own property.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Concessions on, leasing of public property.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>It has been and shall continue to be the policy of the State to authorize Baltimore City to displace or limit competition in the award of concessions on, over or under property owned or leased by the City and in the leasing or subleasing of property owned or leased by the City in order to utilize properly the assets of the City for the best public purpose; to provide necessary or desirable governmental services at the lowest possible cost; to protect the public from unscrupulous business practices and excessive prices; to provide for the accessibility to public property by as many citizens as possible; and to promote the general welfare by utilizing public property for the benefit of the citizens of the community.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Baltimore City has the authority to displace or limit competition by granting one or more franchises for any concession on, over or under property owned, or leased, by the City on an exclusive or nonexclusive basis, to control prices and rates for such franchises; to establish rules and regulations to govern the operation of the franchises and for the enforcement thereof; and to lease or sublease publicly owned or leased land, improvements to land or both on terms to be determined by the City without regard to any anticompetitive effect.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Development and redevelopment.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>It has been and shall continue to be the policy of this State to authorize Baltimore City to displace or limit competition with respect to residential, commercial, industrial, and economic development and redevelopment to ensure the stability and vitality of urban areas.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>In order to achieve this public purpose Baltimore City has been granted the authority to displace or limit competition by limiting or controlling the types and number of uses or projects it will authorize, promote, assist, or permit in exercising its powers to undertake, promote, and regulate, and otherwise control residential, commercial, industrial, and economic development and redevelopment, including but not limited to acquiring, leasing, selling or disposing of, and controlling land, structures, and other property and borrowing money, and making loans or providing other forms of financial assistance and guarantees.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Construction; Scope.</span></p>
<p>The powers granted to Baltimore City pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-58">this section</a> shall not be construed:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>to grant to Baltimore City powers in any substantive area not otherwise granted to the City by other public general or public local law;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>to restrict the City from exercising any power granted to the City by other public general or public local law or otherwise;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>to authorize the City or its officers to engage in any activity which is beyond their power under other public general law, public local law, or otherwise; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>to preempt or supersede the regulatory authority of any State department or agency under any public general law.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 397, Acts of 1983</p>
```


### § (59). Loans and loan guarantees. {#s-59}

```{=html}
<p>To use the proceeds of any debt of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, created pursuant to <a href="article-xi.html#s-7">Article XI, Section 7 of the Constitution of Maryland</a>, in order to effectuate any purpose which the General Assembly of Maryland has or may hereafter authorize pursuant to Articles <a href="article-xi-g.html">XI-G</a>, <a href="article-xi-h.html">XI-H</a>, or <a href="article-xi-i.html">XI-I</a> of the Constitution of Maryland, as follows:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span></p>
<p>to make or contract to make financial loans to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the rehabilitation, renovation, redevelopment, or improvement of buildings or structures located within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for residential purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span></p>
<p>to guarantee or insure financial loans made by third parties to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the rehabilitation, renovation, redevelopment, or improvement of buildings or structures located within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for residential purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span></p>
<p>to make or contract to make financial loans to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the purchase or acquisition of leasehold or fee simple interests in buildings or structures, and for construction, reconstruction, erection, development, rehabilitation, renovation, redevelopment, or improvement of buildings or structures, located within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for commercial purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span></p>
<p>to guarantee or insure financial loans made by third parties to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the purchase or acquisition of leasehold or fee simple interests in buildings or structures, and for construction, reconstruction, erection, development, rehabilitation, renovation, redevelopment, or improvement of buildings or structures, located within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for commercial purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span></p>
<p>to make or contract to make financial loans to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the purchase, acquisition, construction, erection, or development of buildings or structures, including any land necessary therefor, within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for residential purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span></p>
<p>to guarantee or insure financial loans made by third parties to any person or other legal entity which are to be used for or in connection with the purchase, acquisition, construction, erection, or development of buildings or structures, including any land necessary therefor, within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for residential purposes;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span></p>
<p>to make or contract to make financial loans to any person or other legal entity to be used for or in connection with the purchase, acquisition, construction, reconstruction, erection, development, redevelopment, rehabilitation, renovation, modernization, or improvement of buildings or structures, including any land necessary therefor, within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for industrial purposes; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span></p>
<p>to guarantee or insure financial loans made by third parties to any person or other legal entity which are to be used for or in connection with the purchase, acquisition, construction, reconstruction, erection, development, redevelopment, rehabilitation, renovation, modernization, or improvement of buildings or structures, including any land necessary therefor, within the boundaries of Baltimore City, which buildings or structures are to be used or occupied for industrial purposes.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 645, Acts of 1984</p>
```


### § (60). Reports of loans, loan guarantees, and loan insurance. {#s-60}

```{=html}
<p>To exercise powers which may be granted by the General Assembly of Maryland under Articles <a href="article-xi-g.html">XI-G</a>, <a href="article-xi-h.html">XI-H</a>, and <a href="article-xi-i.html">XI-I</a> of the Constitution of Maryland only if the following requirements are fulfilled:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Reports required.</span></p>
<p>Prior to each regular session of the General Assembly of Maryland, the Board of Estimates of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall submit to each member of the General Assembly representing Baltimore City a report regarding loans and loan guarantees made during the immediately preceding fiscal year, from the proceeds of any debt created or credit extended under <a href="article-xi.html#s-7">Article XI, Section 7 of the Constitution of Maryland</a> or from the proceeds of any notes issued in anticipation of such proceeds, for the purposes authorized pursuant to Articles <a href="article-xi-g.html">XI-G</a>, <a href="article-xi-h.html">XI-H</a>, or <a href="article-xi-i.html">XI-I</a> of the Constitution of Maryland.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Contents.</span></p>
<p>The report shall contain the following information regarding each loan of $300,000 or more, made or guaranteed as described in subsection (a); provided that the loans or loan guarantees or insurance for any particular project or the particular project itself may not be divided or split for the purpose of being exempted from the reporting requirement:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the recipient of the loan, and a brief description of the purpose of the loan.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>the street address and a brief description of each property acquired, constructed, rehabilitated or otherwise improved with the proceeds of the loan.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>the amount of each loan made.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>the amount of each loan guaranteed and the amount of reserve maintained for each guarantee commitment.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>the amount and source of any other funds committed in connection with the loan.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>the extent of minority business participation in the proceeds of the loan, determined in accordance with the standards, terms, and conditions of the minority business enterprise program of the Board of Estimates of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>whether and in what manner the provisions of <a href="article-vi.html#s-4">Article VI, Section 4</a> {<a href="article-vi.html#s-11">Article VI, § 11</a>} of the City Charter applied to the loan.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>whether and in what manner Sections 19 through 27 inclusive of the Baltimore City Code, “Contracts - Hours and Wages” {Article 5, Subtitle 25, “Hours and Wages - Service Contracts”, City Code (Edition 2000)}, applied to the loan.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">“Guarantee” defined.</span></p>
<p>In <a href="article-ii.html#s-60">this section</a>, a loan “guarantee” or a loan “guaranteed” shall include insurance of a loan, or a loan insured.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Legislative audit.</span></p>
<p>At the request of either the Speaker of the House and President of the Senate or the Joint Budget and Audit Committee to the General Assembly, the legislative auditor shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>examine, evaluate, and audit any report made under <a href="article-ii.html#s-60">this section</a>; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>examine and evaluate any loan or loan guarantee for which a report is not made in order to determine if a report should be made for it under <a href="article-ii.html#s-60">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Savings clause.</span></p>
<p>Failure to file any report required by <a href="article-ii.html#s-60">this section</a> does not affect the validity of any bonds or other obligations issued for the purpose of exercising any of the powers authorized by Articles XI-G, XI-H, and XI-I of the Constitution.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 749, Acts of 1984</p>
```


### § (61). Downtown Commercial District Management Authority. {#s-61}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Establishment, boundaries, etc.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>To establish a Downtown Commercial District Management Authority within the City of Baltimore to do any or all of the following: promote or market the district; provide supplementary security and maintenance services; and provide amenities in public areas.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>To specify and modify the boundaries of the district but in no event outside the bounds of lines as follows:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>on the north, a line beginning at the Jones Falls Expressway, going west on Centre Street to Park Avenue, then north on Park Avenue to Read Street, then northwest on Read Street to Howard Street, then north on Howard Street to Martin Luther King Boulevard, then southwest on Martin Luther King Boulevard to Eutaw Street, then south on Eutaw Street to Franklin Street, then west to Greene Street;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>on the west, Greene Street and Russell Street;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>on the south, a line running generally westerly from Russell Street and Lee Street to Lee Street and Light Street, and then following Light Street to Key Highway, and then following Key Highway to Lawrence Street; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">4.</span></p>
<p>on the east, the Jones Falls Expressway and President Street.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>Notwithstanding subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, the district may include properties binding on either side of the boundaries authorized under this subsection.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>To specify the powers and functions which may be exercised and conducted by the Authority and the amount of benefit assessment charges which may be imposed on properties in the district.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>To specify the duration of the Authority.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>To provide for the imposition and collection of the taxes or charges, and for disbursement of the revenue therefrom to the Authority.  The financial plan of the Authority, including its annual budget and its tax and fee schedule, shall be subject to approval by the Board of Estimates.  Taxes and charges imposed under this paragraph may not exceed those proposed by the Authority.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>To determine the organization and method of initial appointment of board members of the Authority, the majority of the members of the board shall be owners or representatives of owners of properties in the district that are subject to taxes or charges under <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Powers of Authority.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Contract with Police Department.</span></p>
<p>As provided by ordinance, the Authority shall enter into a contract with the Baltimore Police Department to hire two officers of the Baltimore Police Department to exclusively patrol the 400 unit block of Baltimore Street and the unit block of Custom House Avenue between the hours of 10 p.m. and 3 a.m. on the Thursday, Friday, and Saturday of each week.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">General powers.</span></p>
<p>As provided by ordinance, the Authority may have the power:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>to be a special tax district or special benefits assessment district and to conduct the functions which are assigned to it by the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>to acquire, hold and use property necessary to achieve its purposes.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>to make contracts; to sue and be sued.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>to accept grants.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>to borrow for purposes consistent with the public purposes of the Authority.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vi)</span></p>
<p>to propose in its annual budget the taxes or charges on properties within the district. No such amounts shall be levied against residential property with fewer than four dwelling units.  Property which is exempt under State law from ordinary property taxes shall be exempt from assessments by the district.  Before adopting its proposed budget and before making its recommendation to the City, the Authority shall hold a public hearing on taxes or charges proposed for the district.  The Authority shall publish notice of the hearing in a newspaper of general circulation in Baltimore City at least once a week for three consecutive weeks before the hearing.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vii)</span></p>
<p>to do all things necessary or convenient to carry out its powers.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(viii)</span></p>
<p>to adopt, amend and modify by-laws, all of which shall be subject to the approval of the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ix)</span></p>
<p>to establish and elect officers and provide for their terms and duties.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(x)</span></p>
<p>to contract for and purchase goods and services, not subject to the City requirements regarding wage scales, competitive bidding or other local procurement laws; however the Authority shall be subject to City ordinances and City policy requiring achievement of goals regarding minority and women’s business enterprises.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Limitations.</span></p>
<p>The Authority is subject to the following limitations:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>It is not permitted to exercise any police or general powers other than those authorized by State law and City ordinance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>It may not pledge the full faith or credit of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>It cannot extend its life and it cannot modify its boundaries without City Council approval.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>It cannot impose taxes, fees or assessments in excess of those approved by the Board of Estimates.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>It cannot exercise the power of eminent domain.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>Except as otherwise authorized by law, it cannot engage in competition with the private sector.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>Any fees, charges or taxes collected pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a> shall be used only for the purposes authorized under <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a> and may not revert to the General Fund of the City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>It may not be an agency of the City of Baltimore or the State of Maryland.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(9)</span></p>
<p>Employees of the Authority shall reside in the City of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(10)</span></p>
<p>Subject to the approval of the Board of Estimates, it shall provide an adjustment of any taxes and charges imposed on a specific property pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a> based on the current rate of occupancy of the property.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Considerations.</span></p>
<p>In adopting an ordinance, the City Council shall give consideration to the views of the property owners, the retail merchants, the hotels and motels, the property tenants, and the other members of the business community within the district.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Periodic review.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and City Council shall review the effectiveness and desirability of continuing the existence of any district established under <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a> every 5 years from the enactment of the ordinance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Approval by property owners.</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and City Council shall establish a fair and equitable process for the approval and adoption of an ordinance, under <a href="article-ii.html#s-61">this section</a>, by the property owners who are subject to taxes or charges in the district.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>Editor's Notes, History:</strong> Ch. 604, Acts of 1992; Ch. 36, Acts of 2022; Subsection (b)(1) was added by Chapter 36, Acts of 2022, effective July 1, 2022.,  Section 3 of Chapter 36 provides that the subsection “shall remain effective for a period of 5 years and, at the end of June 30, 2027, ... with no further action required by the General Assembly, shall be abrogated and of no further force and effect.”</p>
```


### § (62). Tax increment financing. {#s-62}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>To borrow money by issuing and selling bonds, at any time and from time to time, for the purpose of financing and refinancing the development of an industrial, commercial, or residential area in Baltimore City.  Such bonds shall be payable from and secured by a pledge of the special fund described in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may also establish sinking funds, establish debt service reserve funds, or pledge other assets and revenues towards the payments of the principal and interest, including revenues received by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore pursuant to a development agreement.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>In lieu of the pledges set forth in paragraph (1) of this subsection, the authorizing ordinance or trust agreement, subject to subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) of this paragraph, may pledge or assign:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>all or any part of that portion of the revenues and receipts from the taxes representing the levy of the tax increment that would normally be paid to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore to the payment of such principal and interest;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>the special fund described in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> and any other fund into which all or any part of such revenues and receipts are deposited after such revenues and receipts are appropriated by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore to the payment of such principal and interest;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">3.</span></p>
<p>amounts provided to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by the State under § 2-222 the Tax–Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">4.</span></p>
<p>any other assets and revenues of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>The revenues and receipts may not be irrevocably pledged to the payment of such principal and interest and the obligation to pay such principal and interest from such revenues and receipts shall be subject to annual appropriation by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may not pledge its full faith and credit or unlimited taxing power to the payment of such bonds.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Definitions.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>In <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> the following words have the meanings indicated, unless the context clearly indicates another or different meaning or intent:</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>“Abandoned property” has the meaning stated in § 21-17(a) of the Public Local Laws of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>“Adjusted assessable base” means, for real property that qualifies for farm or agricultural use under <a href="article-gtp.html#s-8-209">§ 8-209 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>, as amended, replaced, or supplemented from time to time, the fair market value of the property without regard to its agricultural use assessment as of January 1 of that year preceding the effective date of the ordinance creating the development district under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>“Affordable housing” means housing that is affordable to households with incomes up to 115% of the regional median income.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>“Assessable base” means the total assessable base of all real property in a development district subject to taxation as determined by the Supervisor of Assessments.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>“Assessment ratio” means any real property tax assessment ratio, however designated or calculated, which is used or applied under applicable general law in determining the assessable base.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>“Assessment ratio” includes the assessment percentage as provided under <a href="article-gtp.html#s-8-103">§ 8-103(c) of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>, as amended, replaced, or supplemented from time to time.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>“Bonds” or “bond” means any bonds or bond, notes or note, or other similar instruments or instrument issued by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore pursuant to and in accordance with <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>“Development” includes new development, redevelopment, revitalization, and renovation.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(9)</span></p>
<p>“Development agreement” means an agreement between the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore and any person involved in or responsible for development of property within a development district pursuant to which such person shall agree to pay in each year in which any bonds are outstanding an amount equal to all or a portion of the debt service on bonds issued pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> to finance or refinance development in such development district.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(10)</span></p>
<p>“Development district” means an area or areas within the City of Baltimore designated by an ordinance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(11)</span></p>
<p>“Distressed property” has the meaning stated in § 21-17(a) of the Public Local Laws of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(12)</span></p>
<p>“Original assessable base” means the assessable base as of January 1 of that year preceding the effective date of the ordinance creating the development district under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(13)</span></p>
<p>“Original full cash value” means the dollar amount which is determined by dividing the original assessable base by the assessment ratio used to determine the original assessable base.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(14)</span></p>
<p>“Original taxable value” means for any tax year the dollar amount that is the lesser of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the product of the original full cash value times the assessment ratio applicable to that tax year;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the original assessable base; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>if an adjusted assessable base applies, then the “original taxable value” is the adjusted assessable base.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(15)</span></p>
<p>“Supervisor of Assessments” means the Supervisor of Assessments for Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(16)</span></p>
<p>“Tax increment” means for any tax year the amount by which the assessable base as of January 1 preceding that tax year exceeds the original taxable value, divided by the assessment ratio used to determine the original taxable value.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(17)</span></p>
<p>“Tax year” means the period from July 1 of a calendar year through June 30 of the next calendar year.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(18)</span></p>
<p>“State obligations” means any bonds or bond, notes or note, or other similar instruments or instrument issued by the Maryland Economic Development Corporation, the State of Maryland, or any agency, department, or political subdivision thereof, the proceeds of which have been used for any of the purposes specified in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (c) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Application of proceeds.</span></p>
<p>All proceeds received from any bonds issued and sold pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> shall be applied solely for:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>the cost of purchasing, leasing, condemning, or otherwise acquiring land or other property, or an interest in them, in the designated development district area or as necessary for a right-of-way or other easement to or from the development district area;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>site removal;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>surveys and studies;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>relocation of businesses or residents;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>installation of utilities, construction of parks and playgrounds, and other necessary improvements including streets and roads to, from, or within the development district, lighting, and other facilities;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>construction or rehabilitation of buildings provided that such buildings:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>are to be devoted to a governmental use or purpose;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>are abandoned property;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>are distressed property; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>will provide units of affordable housing;</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>reserves and capitalized interest on the bonds;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>necessary costs of issuing bonds;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(9)</span></p>
<p>structured and surface parking facilities that are:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>publicly owned; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>privately owned but serve a public purpose; and</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(10)</span></p>
<p>payment of the principal and interest on loans, money advanced, or indebtedness incurred by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore for any of the purposes set out in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(d)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Prerequisites for bond issuance.</span></p>
<p>Before issuing any bonds under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>, the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>designate by ordinance an area or areas within the City of Baltimore as a “development district”;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>receive from the Supervisor of Assessments a certification as to the amount of the original assessable base, or if applicable, the adjusted assessable base; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>provide that until the bonds have been fully paid or thereafter, the property taxes on real property within the development district shall be divided as follows:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>that portion of the taxes which would be produced by the rate at which taxes levied each year by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore upon the original taxable value shall be allocated to and when collected paid into the funds of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore in the same manner as taxes by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore on all other property are paid; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>that portion of the taxes representing the levy on the tax increment that would normally be paid to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall be paid into a special fund to be applied in accordance with the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (e) of this section</a>.  This yield shall not be considered as municipal taxes for the purposes of any constant yield tax limitation or State or local restriction.  No State real property taxes may be paid into the special fund.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(e)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Special fund.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may enact an ordinance creating a special fund described in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> with respect to a development district, even though no bonds authorized by <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> have been issued by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore with respect to that development district or are then outstanding.  The taxes allocated to such special fund by <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> shall thereafter be paid over to such special fund, as long as such ordinance remains in effect.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>When no bonds authorized by <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> are outstanding with respect to a development district and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by ordinance so determines, moneys in the special fund for that development district created pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> may be:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>used for any of the purposes described in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (c) of this section</a>;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>accumulated for payment of debt service on bonds subsequently issued under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>used to pay or to reimburse the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore for debt service which the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore is obligated to pay or has paid (whether such obligation is general or limited) on any bonds or State obligations; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>paid to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore to provide funds to be used for any legal purpose as may be determined by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>When any bonds authorized by <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> are outstanding with respect to a development district and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore so determines, moneys in the special fund for that development district created pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d)(3)(ii) of this section</a> may be used as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection in any fiscal year by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, but only to the extent that:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the amount in such special fund exceeds the unpaid debt service payable on such bonds in such fiscal year and is not restricted so as to prohibit the use of such moneys; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>such use is not prohibited by the ordinance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore or resolution of the Board of Finance authorizing the issuance of such bonds.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(f)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Enabling ordinance.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Before issuing any bonds under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall enact an ordinance which:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>specifies and describes the proposed undertaking and states that it has complied with <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d) of this section</a>; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>specifies the maximum principal amount of bonds to be issued, from time to time or at any time, pursuant to such ordinance.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The ordinance, if such bonds constitute debt of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore under <a href="article-xi.html#s-7">Section 7 of Article XI</a> of the State Constitution, shall be submitted to the legal voters of the City of Baltimore at the time and place specified therein.  Such ordinance shall become effective only if it is approved by the majority of the votes cast at the time and place specified in such ordinance.  Except as otherwise provided herein, <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> may not be construed as requiring the submission to the legal voters of the City of Baltimore of any ordinance creating a development district pursuant to <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (d) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>Such ordinance may specify that the bonds authorized thereunder may be issued from time to time or at any time.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>Such ordinance may authorize the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by ordinance or the Board of Finance by resolution to specify and prescribe any of the following as it deems appropriate to effect the financing or refinancing of the proposed undertaking:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>the actual principal amount of the bonds to be issued;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>the actual rate or rates of interest the bonds are to bear or the method for determining the same;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the manner in which and the terms upon which the bonds are to be sold;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>the manner in which and the times and places that the interest on the bonds is to be paid;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>the time or times that the bonds may be executed, issued, and delivered;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vi)</span></p>
<p>the form and tenor of the bonds and the denominations in which the bonds may be issued;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vii)</span></p>
<p>the manner in which and the times and places that the principal of the bonds is to be paid, within the limitations sot forth in this subsection;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(viii)</span></p>
<p>provisions pursuant to which any or all of the bonds may be called for redemption prior to their stated maturity dates;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ix)</span></p>
<p>the terms and provisions of any development agreement to be executed by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore and any person in connection with the issuance of such bonds; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(x)</span></p>
<p>any other provisions not inconsistent with <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>, the Charter and applicable law as shall be determined by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore or the Board of Finance (as the case may be) to be necessary or desirable to effect the financing or refinancing of the proposed undertaking.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(g)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Tax exemption.</span></p>
<p>The principal amount of the bonds, the interest payable thereon, their transfer, and any income derived therefrom, including any profit made in the sale or transfer thereof, shall be exempt from taxation by the State of Maryland and by the several counties and municipalities of the State of Maryland but shall be included, to the extent required under <a href="article-gtg.html">Title 8, Subtitle 2 of the Tax-General Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>, as amended, replaced, or supplemented from time to time, in computing the net earnings of financial institutions.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(h)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Form; Tenor; Sale.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>All bonds may be in bearer form or in coupon form or may be registrable as to principal alone or as to both principal and interest.  Each of the bonds shall be deemed to be a “security” within the meaning of <a href="article-gcl.html#s-8-102">§ 8-102 of the Commercial Law Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>, as amended, replaced, or supplemented from time to time, whether or not it is either one or a class or series or by its terms is divisible into a class or series of instruments.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>All bonds shall be signed manually or in facsimile by the Mayor of the City of Baltimore, and the seal of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore shall be impressed thereon manually or by facsimile and attested by the custodian of the City seal, manually or by facsimile.  If any officer whose signature or countersignature appears on the bonds ceases to be such officer before delivery of the bonds, his signature or countersignature shall nevertheless be valid and sufficient for all purposes the same as if he had remained in office until delivery thereof.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>All bonds shall mature not later than 40 years from their date of issuance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>All bonds shall be sold in such manner, either at public or private sale, and upon such terms as the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by ordinance or (if authorized in the ordinance authorizing such bonds) the Board of Finance by resolution deems best.  Any contract for the acquisition of property may provide that payment shall be in bonds.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Refunding bonds.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>The Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, acting by and through the Board of Finance thereof, is hereby authorized and empowered to issue its bonds for the purpose of refunding any bonds authorized to be issued under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> by payment at maturity or the purchase or redemption of bonds in advance of maturity.  The validity of any refunding bonds shall in no way be dependent upon or related to the validity or invalidity of the bonds being refunded.  Such refunding bonds may be issued by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, acting by and through the Board of Finance thereof, for the purpose of providing it with funds to pay any of its outstanding bonds authorized to be issued under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> at maturity, to purchase in the open market any of its outstanding bonds authorized to be issued under the provisions of this subsection prior to their maturity, to redeem prior to their maturity any outstanding bonds which are, by their terms, redeemable, to pay interest on any outstanding bonds prior to their payment at maturity or purchase or redemption in advance of maturity, or to pay any redemption or purchase premium in connection with the refunding of any of its outstanding bonds authorized to be issued under the provisions of this subsection.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> may be issued for the public purpose of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>realizing savings to Baltimore City in the aggregate cost of debt service on either a direct comparison or present value basis; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>debt restructuring that:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>in the aggregate effects such a reduction in the cost of debt service; or</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>is determined by the Board of Finance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore to be in the best interest of Baltimore City, to be consistent with Baltimore City’s long-term financial plan, and to realize a financial objective of Baltimore City, including, without limitation, improving the relationship of debt service to a source of payment such as taxes, assessments, or other charges.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> may be issued in whatever principal amount shall be required to achieve the purpose for the issuance of the refunding bonds, which amount may be in excess of the principal amount of the bonds refunded or the maximum principal amount of bonds authorized to be issued under <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">subsection (f)(4)(i) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> may be issued to mature on such dates and in such amounts as the Board of Finance may determine; provided that the entire principal amount represented by the refunding bonds shall be discharged not more than 40 years from the date of issuance of the bonds being refunded.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> may be sold at public sale by the solicitation of competitive bids or at private (negotiated) sale without advertisement or solicitation of competitive bids, for a price or prices which may be at, above, or below the par value of the refunding bonds, as determined by resolution of the Board of Finance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.  If the Board of Finance determines to sell the refunding bonds at public sale, the refunding bonds shall be sold to the highest responsible bidder or bidders therefor after due notice of such sale, but the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, acting by and through the Board of Finance thereof, shall have the right to reject any or all bids therefor for any reason.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> shall bear interest at such rate or rates as may be determined by the Board of Finance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, which rate or rates may be fixed or variable or as determined by a method approved by the Board of Finance, and such interest shall be payable at such time or times as may be determined by the Board of Finance.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>The proceeds of the sale of any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>, after the payment of issuance costs relating thereto, shall be set aside by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore as a separate trust fund to be used solely for the purposes stated in this subsection.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(8)</span></p>
<p>Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the powers granted in, the limitations and obligations imposed by, and the procedures specified in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> with respect to the issuance of bonds shall be applicable to the issuance of refunding bonds.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(9)</span></p>
<p>Any refunding bonds authorized to be issued and sold under the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a> shall not be subject to any debt policy limitation that may from time to time be established by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(j)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Assessment and taxation of property.</span></p>
<p>Whenever the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, as lessor, leases its property within the development district, the property shall be assessed and taxed in the same manner as privately owned property, and the lease or contract shall provide that the lessee shall pay taxes or payments in lieu of taxes upon the assessed value of the entire property and not merely the assessed value of the leasehold interest.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(k)</span></p>
<p>In addition to the powers in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>, the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may use the authority granted to a  political subdivision for tax increment financing in a sustainable community as provided for in <a href="article-gec.html">Title 12, Subtitle 2 of the Economic Development Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(l)</span></p>
<p>In addition to the powers in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">this section</a>, the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may use the authority granted to a political subdivision for tax increment financing in a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise zone as provided for in <a href="article-gec.html">Title 12, Subtitle 2 of the Economic Development Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland</a>.</p>
</div>
<p class="charter-history"><strong>History:</strong> Ch. 624, Acts of 1994; Chs. 9 and 10, Acts of 1996; Ch. 66, Acts of 2000; Ch. 170, Acts of 2001; Ch. 405, Acts of 2004; Ch. 338, Acts of 2008; Ch. 544, Acts of 2008; Ch. 624, Acts of 2013; Chs. 530 and 531, Acts of 2014</p>
```


### § (62A). Special Tax Districts. {#s-62a}

```{=html}
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(a)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">In general.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>Subject to the provisions of <a href="article-ii.html#s-62a">this section</a> and for the purpose stated in paragraph (2) of this subsection, to:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>create a special taxing district;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>levy ad valorem or special taxes; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>issue bonds and other obligations.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>The purpose of the authority granted under paragraph (1) of this subsection is to provide financing, refinancing, or reimbursement for the cost of the design, construction, establishment, extension, alteration, or acquisition of infrastructure improvements, whether situated within the special taxing district or outside the special taxing district if the infrastructure improvement is reasonably related to other infrastructure improvements within the special taxing district.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(b)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Definitions.</span></p>
<p>In <a href="article-ii.html#s-62a">this section</a> the following words have the meanings indicated, unless the context clearly indicates another or different meaning or intent:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
<p>“Abandoned property” has the meaning stated in § 21-17(a) of the Public Local Laws of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(2)</span></p>
<p>“Affordable housing” has the meaning stated in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62">§ (62)(b) of this article</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(3)</span></p>
<p>“Bond” means a special obligation bond, revenue bond, note, or other similar instrument issued by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore in accordance with <a href="article-ii.html#s-62a">this section</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(4)</span></p>
<p>“Cost” includes the cost of:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>construction, reconstruction, and renovation and purchasing, leasing, condemning, or otherwise acquiring any lands, structures, real or personal property, rights, rights-of-way, franchises, easements, and interests acquired or to be acquired by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>all machinery and equipment including machinery and equipment needed to expand or enhance city services to the special taxing district;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>financing charges and interest prior to and during construction, and, if deemed advisable by the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, for a limited period after completion of the construction, interest and reserves for principal and interest, including costs of municipal bond insurance and any other type of financial guaranty and costs of issuance;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iv)</span></p>
<p>extensions, enlargements, additions, and improvements;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(v)</span></p>
<p>architectural, engineering, financial, and legal services;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vi)</span></p>
<p>plans, specifications, studies, surveys, and estimates of cost and of revenues;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(vii)</span></p>
<p>administrative expenses necessary or incident to determining to proceed with the infrastructure improvements;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(viii)</span></p>
<p>site removal;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ix)</span></p>
<p>relocation of businesses and residents; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(x)</span></p>
<p>other expenses as may be necessary or incident to the construction, acquisition, and financing of the infrastructure improvements.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(5)</span></p>
<p>“Distressed property”  has the meaning stated in § 21-17(a) of the Public Local Laws of Baltimore City.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(6)</span></p>
<p>“Infrastructure improvement” means adequate storm drainage systems, sewers, water systems, roads, bridges, culverts, tunnels, streets, sidewalks, lighting, surface parking, playgrounds, parks and recreation facilities, libraries, schools, transit facilities, solid waste facilities, buildings devoted to a governmental use or purpose, buildings that are abandoned property or distressed property, buildings that provide units of affordable housing, structured parking facilities that are publicly owned or privately owned, but serve a public purpose, and other infrastructure improvements as necessary for the development and utilization of the land, with respect to any defined geographic region within the City of Baltimore.</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(7)</span></p>
<p>“State obligations” means any bonds or bond, notes or note, or other similar instruments or instrument issued by the Maryland Economic Development Corporation, the State of Maryland, or any agency, department, or political subdivision thereof, provided:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(i)</span></p>
<p>such bonds are issued for the purposes specified in <a href="article-ii.html#s-62a">subsection (a)(2) of this section</a>;</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(ii)</span></p>
<p>a request has been made to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore by both:</p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">1.</span></p>
<p>the owners of at least two–thirds of the assessed valuation of the real property located within the special taxing district; and</p>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-4">
<p><span class="charter-num">2.</span></p>
<p>at least two–thirds of the owners of the real property located within the special taxing district, provided that multiple owners of a single parcel are treated as a single owner; and a single owner of multiple parcels is treated as one owner; and</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-3">
<p><span class="charter-num">(iii)</span></p>
<p>the proceeds of such bonds have been applied in accordance with <a href="article-ii.html#s-62a">subsection (d) of this section</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-1">
<p><span class="charter-num">(c)</span> <span class="charter-subhead">Bond issuance on request.</span></p>
<div class="charter-para charter-depth-2">
<p><span class="charter-num">(1)</span></p>
```
